timing: Registered before inspecting any instrument TRAIN/DEV outcome, after fixing real source membership. Execute only if the primary instrument-label task has no paid frontend simultaneously eligible on TRAIN and DEV. Preserve primary results and keep its TEST closed.
question: When the instrument is already known, can the system identify which of two real reference performance recordings a later passage comes from, and decide when to buy the query video? This is a separate retrieval target. Source identity varies by split. No claim of cross-source transfer for identity labels themselves: the transferable mechanism compares an unfamiliar query with two unfamiliar reference exemplars.
construction: Within each split and each instrument, sort works by numeric Commons page id. The earliest frozen excerpt per work is a reference, never a query. Use each remaining disjoint excerpt once. The positive is the earlier exemplar from the same production. The deterministic next work in the within-instrument cyclic list supplies the negative. Require >=2 distinct creators per class; no use of TEST references during selection/training. Exemplar videos are in a precomputed known gallery; the query's pixels remain paid. Query and reference video/audio intervals never overlap. Candidate order alternates by query index plus local recording rank, independent of acoustic or visual outcomes. Fixed creator grouping/familywise interpretation as in the main protocol.
matchers: FREE and paid matchers compare standardized absolute per-dimension differences between the query and each reference at equal-duration prefixes. Standardizers fit on TRAIN sources for external splits. TRAIN query standardization and supervised weights exclude BOTH creators touched by the query pair. When only one same-instrument training work remains, fixed equal-distance weights are used for whichever action has no eligible disjoint TRAIN pairs. For each channel compare (1) equal weighted antipodal distance and (2) supervised pairwise ridge metric on disjoint TRAIN positive/negative pairs. Common FREE audio uses the signed supervised distance advantage with an equal-distance prior, never candidate ID or pixels. Paid candidates in fixed order are equal-weight visual distance and supervised visual distance. No ImageNet instrument logits for within-instrument identity. Use the original .30 paid price, .40 rate, .20 discount, eligibility thresholds, DEV ranking, 66-arm policy protocol and independent verification.
inference: Queries share references and negative production identity. Report raw creator-macro and the paired outcomes, and explicitly cluster connected components sharing either reference within each split/instrument for uncertainty. This can leave as few as two independent complexes in TEST and cannot establish population-level timing superiority. Withhold scientific confirmation unless TRAIN and DEV pay-gain gates pass. No test-driven change of primary task, prices, data, weights or reference definitions.
